chunks: “The people of major sins, all of them, when the hadd is carried out upon them twice, they are killed on the third time.”
12 - ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ādam ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī, who said:

I was with Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام when a letter from Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik came to him concerning a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and had intercourse with her. For indeed the people have disagreed with us concerning this: one group said, ‘Kill him,’ and another group said, ‘Burn him.’

So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام wrote to him: “Indeed, the sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living. His hadd is that his hand be cut off for his grave-digging and stripping of the clothes, and the hadd for zina is to be carried out upon him: if he was muḥṣan, he is stoned; and if he was not muḥṣan, he is flogged one hundred times.”
And Yūnus has narrated what we mentioned from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.أُحْصِنَ: being muḥṣan, meaning legally protected by prior valid marriage status in the hadd context
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse subject to hadd punishment
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the prescribed legal punishment in Islamic law
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: major sins that incur serious legal and moral consequences
key_terms.رُجِمَ: was stoned as the prescribed hadd punishment
key_terms.نَبَشَ: dug up a grave or exhumed the dead

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for violating a grave and committing zina with a deceased woman in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses legal punishments concerning repeated major offenses and a specific case involving violation of a deceased woman’s grave and body. It establishes that the sanctity of the dead is equivalent to the sanctity of the living, and assigns separate hadd penalties for grave desecration, theft of clothing, and zina according to the offender’s legal status.
